question: Which Indian boxer was penalized for refusing a medal ceremony in the 2014 Asian Games?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarita Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indian boxer **Sarita Devi** was penalized for refusing to accept the bronze medal during the medal ceremony at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon, South Korea.
 
• The controversy erupted when Sarita Devi lost her semi-final bout against South Korea’s Park Ji-na in the women's lightweight (60 kg) category under dubious circumstances.
 
• Sarita protested against the biased decision of the judges, which was widely criticized by the boxing community and spectators.
 
• During the medal ceremony, Sarita refused to wear the bronze medal and instead handed it over to her opponent as a mark of protest.
 
• The International Boxing Association (AIBA) took strict action and imposed a one-year ban on Sarita Devi for her actions, citing a breach of sportsmanship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijender Singh**

 
 
• Vijender Singh is a celebrated Indian boxer and an Olympic bronze medalist in the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
 
• He is known for his remarkable achievements in amateur and professional boxing, but was not involved in any controversies at the 2014 Asian Games.
 
 
 
• **Mary Kom**
 
 
• Mary Kom, also known as "Magnificent Mary," is a six-time world champion and an Olympic bronze medalist in boxing.
 
• She competed in the 2014 Asian Games and won a gold medal in the women’s flyweight (51 kg) category.
 
• Mary Kom is one of the most successful Indian athletes, but was not involved in the mentioned incident.
 
 
 
• **Nikhat Zareen**
 
 
• Nikhat Zareen is a rising star in Indian boxing and became a world champion in 2022 in the women’s flyweight category.
 
• She did not participate in the 2014 Asian Games and is unrelated to the controversy involving Sarita Devi.
 
 
 
• **19th Asian Games, 2023**:
 
 
• Held in Hangzhou, **China**.
 
• China topped the list with 383 total medals, followed by Japan (188), South Korea (190).
 
• India ranked 4th with 107 medals, of which 28 Gold, 38 Silver, and 41 Bronze.
